subject: Zenith Health - retry amplification causing regional throughput collapse
messages:
From: Sophie Kim <sophie.kim@zenithhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Ops <infra@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Increased 5xx + retries — throughput collapse in us-east-1

Lukas,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and client-side retry amplification across our East US fleet (us-east-1) starting ~08:55 PST. Throughput dropped by ~65% as retries saturate our connection pool; users are getting long tails on requests and some pipelines have timed out. We're attaching a small sample of request ids and a condensed log.

Key facts:
- Error rate: 5xx from 0.4% -> 6.2% in 10m
- Per-request latency median up from 120ms -> 610ms
- Retries: many clients are retrying aggressively (exponential backoff not observed)

Can Redwood do any routing or immediate mitigation? We need a short-term mitigation (route away, throttle retries at the edge) and a longer-term RCA. We will take a conference call if helpful.

Attaching: zenith_debug_logs_1102.txt

Thanks,
Sophie Kim
Head of Platform, Zenith Health
----
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Kim <sophie.kim@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Increased 5xx + retries — throughput collapse in us-east-1

Sophie,

Thanks for the quick heads up and the logs — we've triaged the sample. Short summary from our side: we're seeing a spike in transient 503s coming from a subset of routers handling cache misses; client retries appear to be amplifying the load (multiple retries per original request). Immediate mitigations we can perform now:

1) Route traffic from affected customers to our us-west-2 pool (cold path) with session affinity off — will add ~30–50ms p50 but avoids the overloaded routers.
2) Apply a temporary per-customer concurrent request throttle at the edge for Zenith to cap retry amplification (configurable to target your error rate SLA).
3) Enable prefix/KV cache warm-up for popular keys in the us-east-1 cohort to reduce cache-miss pressure (10–15m window).

We need explicit authorization to change routing for traffic carrying your prod account due to change control. Sophie, can you confirm go-ahead for the us-west-2 geo-route + throttling? If yes, we'll execute within 7–12 minutes and circle back with telemetry. I've opened an incident runbook and attached a small route dump.

Docs & links:
- Runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/zenith/incident-1102
- Proposed route dump: redwood_route_dump.png (attached)

If your execs want to join a call, Rishi and I can be on it. Also flagging Aditya for pricing/credits discussion if this becomes a prolonged outage.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Agree on route + throttle. Quick notes from infra:
- We'll spin up 6 extra shards in us-west-2 with a warm KV preload; expected readiness ~9–11 minutes.
- Also enabling a short-lived 95th-percentile-based circuit breaker on the us-east-1 router cluster for Zenith traffic only.
- We'll capture traces for the retry loops; ask infra to mark request ids starting with ZEN- to collect detailed traces.

I recommend we do the route first (fail-open to us-west-2) then apply throttles so we don't create a synchronized retry spike. I'll be on the call.
